summary: Alfred Simson describes journeys into the Oriente, the forest province east of the Andes, made in the 1870s. He travels from Guayaquil over the mountains to Riobamba and Baños, then on foot and by canoe past the Jívaros to Canelos and the Napo, and stays for a long time at the village of Aguano among the Napo and Záparo Indians. He goes down the Napo and the Aguarico to the Amazon, and then, at the invitation of the Colombian Rafael Reyes, commands a Brazilian government launch on a voyage up the Putumayo to test whether the river can be navigated. Chapters on the geography of Ecuador and the history of its eastern province, and a closing historical sketch of the country, stand among the travel chapters. Appendices give a short Záparo vocabulary, Piojé words, and heights of mountains and towns.
